page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks reveal a significant performance drop when transitioning from small cached blocks (164.23 GB/sec, bottom 25%) to large uncached blocks (20.9 GB/sec read and 18.67 GB/sec write), with the large block read performance falling into the bottom 10%. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 10% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r5.xlarge offers high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed compute or high memory bandwidth. However, the trade-off is lower overall processing throughput and slower memory access speeds compared to newer hardware generations. This instance is best suited for workloads such as caching layers, Redis databases with moderate throughput requirements (achieving 2.85 million SET operations per second in testing), and lightweight memory-intensive applications that are not sensitive to CPU latency.
